references.text: Isaiah prophesies that when the Messiah comes, the eyes of the blind will be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped—exactly the signs Jesus performs in Luke 7:21.
Isaiah describes the anointed one who will proclaim good news to the poor, bind up the brokenhearted, and give sight to the blind—the messianic program Jesus refers to.
Isaiah prophesies that the deaf will hear and the eyes of the blind will see, pointing forward to Jesus' healings.
Jesus reads from Isaiah in the synagogue at Nazareth and declares that he has come to give sight to the blind and set the oppressed free—his program statement confirmed in 7:21.
In the verse immediately following, Jesus himself summarizes the signs he has just performed: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed—in answer to John the Baptist.
The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus answers John's disciples by pointing to the same healings: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed.
Matthew describes Jesus' extensive healing ministry, where he healed every kind of disease and sickness among the people, paralleling the description in Luke 7:21.
Jesus drives out evil spirits and heals all who were sick, fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy—the same type of activity described in Luke 7:21.
Jesus healed many who suffered from various diseases and drove out many evil spirits, directly parallel to the description in Luke 7:21.
People came to hear Jesus and be healed of their diseases, including those troubled by unclean spirits—a parallel to the healings described in 7:21.
Peter summarizes Jesus' ministry: God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and power, and he went about doing good and healing all who were under the power of the devil.
Peter testifies that Jesus of Nazareth was a man accredited by God through powerful deeds, wonders, and signs—the healings in Luke 7:21 are examples of this.
Jesus urges people to believe because of his works, even if they do not believe his words—his healings serve as proof of his messianic identity.
